open_questions.Q4: IS 17494:2025 (ISO 24444:2019, MOD) exists and is 'Active', with 0 amendments, under BIS committee PCD 19 (https://standardsbis.bsbedge.com/BIS_SearchStandard.aspx?Standard_Number=IS%2017494&id=0). It is NOT made mandatory by the Cosmetics Rules 2020. The Ninth Schedule ('cosmetics in finished form shall conform to the Indian Standards') lists 37 product standards (e.g. Skin Creams IS 6608, Shampoo IS 7884). It has no sunscreen or SPF test-method standard, and the 2025 amendment (G.S.R. 513(E), 29 Jul 2025) did not change that Schedule (https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2022/cos_rules/Cosmetics%20Rules%202020.pdf; https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/resources/UploadCDSCOWeb/2018/UploadGazette_NotificationsFiles/2025.07.29_G.S.R.%20513(E)_Certain%20amendments%20in%20Cosmetics%20Rule%202020.pdf). No Quality Control Order covering it could be confirmed: BIS's compulsory-certification page (https://www.bis.gov.in/product-certification/products-under-compulsory-certification/) rendered without its product list, so a QCO cannot be ruled out from primary text, though cosmetics are licensed by CDSCO/States rather than BIS. Conclusion: best-practice substantiation standard, not shown to be mandatory. Ambiguity for legal: the Ninth Schedule note says 'new or amended standards published by the Bureau of Indian Standards ... shall be mandatory to the cosmetics after six months'; read in context it applies to the listed product standards. PA and water-resistance test methods are still open. US: 'Water Resistant (40/80 minutes)' per 21 CFR 201.327.
open_questions.Q11: No notified amendment adding fairness, premature ageing or greying to the DMR Schedule was found in any primary source opened. (1) The government-hosted DMR Act copies (CBFC https://cbfcindia.gov.in/cbfcAdmin/assets/pdf/Drugs.pdf and Tamil Nadu Drugs Control https://drugscontrol.tn.gov.in/pages/application_forms/dmr_drug_objectional_advertisement_act.pdf) show a Schedule with Leucoderma, Lupus, Obesity etc. and none of those terms. (2) CDSCO's Gazette Notifications list (494 entries to Sep 2026, https://cdsco.gov.in/opencms/opencms/en/Notifications/Gazette-Notifications/) has no DMR amendment. (3) ASCI's AdLaw Compendium (Mar 2026, https://www.ascionline.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/The-AdLaw-Compendium.pdf) describes the DMRA with no Schedule expansion. Caveat: the canonical India Code PDF (https://www.indiacode.nic.in/indiacode/bitstream/123456789/18563/1/the_drugs_and_magic_remedies_(objectionable_advertisements)_act,_1954.pdf) was unreachable (504/timeouts), and no page I opened mentions the 2020 draft at all. Status: treat as NOT notified; keep anti-ageing/brightening wording under the existing cosmetic-claim rules, and re-check India Code when it is reachable.

new_rule_candidates.quote: Labelling is mandatory in advertisements which contain SGC in a manner that materially influences consumer decisions, and the lack of a disclosure label would mislead consumers. ... Examples include: Using synthetically generated influencers and ambassadors.
new_rule_candidates.why_it_matters_for_a_skincare_ad: The tool generates AI people, hands and settings. From around 17-29 Dec 2026, an India ad showing an AI-generated model, presenter or 'creator', or a fabricated setting that shapes how the product is understood, needs a visible label such as 'Created using AI'. No existing rule checks for this label. The house AI mark lives in lib/image_prompt_check.js, not in brand_rules.json.
new_rule_candidates.suggested_pattern_or_check: computed: if the creative metadata marks any person, face, voice or result-setting as AI-generated, require a label matching /\b(created|generated|enhanced)\s+(using|with|by)\s+AI\b|AI[- ]generated/i on the visual (not only in the caption); also require 'Sponsored by <brand>' wording for paid AI-assistant placements.

new_rule_candidates.quote: Fabricating endorsements or testimonials i.e. using AI to create, alter or attribute an endorsement or testimonial in a manner that falsely represents that a real person has used, experienced, approved, recommended or endorsed a product or service when they have not.
new_rule_candidates.why_it_matters_for_a_skincare_ad: These are prohibited even with an AI label. That covers AI-voiced or AI-faced 'customer reviews', AI 'dermatologist' presenters, and AI-made result or after-skin imagery. CLM-21 (testimonial) and CLM-15 (before/after) are only 'fix' and don't know whether the asset is synthetic.
